sentences.text:
Shri Ankit Saxena - Advocate for applicant.
 Shri Yogesh Dhande - Govt. Advocate for respondent/State.
 Shri Nitin Agrawal - Advocate for objector.

Order 
This is the second bail application filed under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 on behalf of applicant for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.142/2024, registered at Police Station-Crime Branch, District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 409,
420, 120-B, 201, 467, 468 and 471 of Indian Penal Code.

2. Learned counsel appearing for applicant submitted that applicant is said to have conducted audit between 06.02.2024 to 09.02.2024 in Bank and being auditor he did not report about the missing gold packets.
It is submitted that applicant has not committed any offence and he was not involved in offence.
At best it can be said that applicant is negligent in his duty.
Applicant is in jail for about six months.
Investigation is complete and charge-sheet has been filed.
Applicant will attend the trial regularly.
Counsel NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:46128 2 MCRC-38374-2024 for applicant also submitted that there is no audit report of applicant on record.
In absence of any evidence, he cannot be kept in jail unnecessarily for long time.
In these circumstances, applicant be released on bail.
3. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondent/State as well as counsel appearing for objector opposed the application for grant of bail.

It is submitted that huge scam has been Dharmendra Dhobi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106135711/
1 committed by applicant acting hand in glove with other co-accused persons, who were employees of Bank and other persons.

sentences.text: Offence is serious in nature.
In these circumstances, applicant may not be released on bail.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
5.
On going through facts and circumstances of the case, it is found that investigation in the case is complete.
Applicant is in jail since 06.03.2024 for about six months.
Applicant is no longer required for custodial investigation in the case.
Objection is also raised that applicant is not resident of Madhya Pradesh, therefore, he may not be available in trial.

6. Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, bail application filed by the applicant is allowed on following conditions:-
(i) Applicant will furnish two local sureties for his appearance before the trial Court.
(ii) Applicant will not leave the country and if he is having passport, he will surrender the same before trial Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:46128 3 MCRC-38374-2024 7.

It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on aforesaid conditions on furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with two local solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for his regular appearance before Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of trial.

8. The applicant shall also abide by the following conditions of Section 480 (3) of B.N.S.S. as under:-
(a) that such person shall attend in accordance with the conditions of the bond executed under this Chapter;
(b) that such person shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which the is accused, or suspected of the commission of which they are suspected and;
(c) that such person shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
9. C.C. as per rules.
(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE sp/-
